“I am immensely sorry that, for the first time since I have been writing to you, I must tell you certain things, which I would like you to take as warnings and corrections, all to the advantage of your soul. Dear Jesus, what you must have suffered to see yourself mistreated even by one of your brides, when in these days (it was carnival) you are already burdened enough with piercings! Daughter, tell me. Does your heart not yet have any beat for your beloved and beautiful Jesus? Do your eyes not look upon him crucified; who has reduced him to such a state, do you know? Our wickedness! […] So, dear Jesus, in these days such torments of sorrow are renewed for you. Now, from one of your Brides I see so laconically suggested a deviation from that small abstinence which your dear Grandmother St. Anne put in the holy Rules of her Daughters, the depriving oneself of eating fatty foods on the last two days of this diabolical worldly amusement, so that with this small abstinence some minimal sorrow might be repaired. In truth, on hearing the Superior read that little note, which contained certain expressions concerning me, I felt myself shudder. My God! Has this daughter ever seen this poor Mother of hers deviate from the least of the holy Rules? […] I am and will be, with God’s help, most rigorous, and will never make the slightest concession. I hope that there you kept the fast, and I would be very much surprised if the poor Community had deviated merely with your permission. Come, then, let us suppose that it was all done through inadvertence, and let us hope that it will never happen again. I assure you that this is the second day I am up, and very unwell, weak as never before. It was a pill of wormwood that I had to swallow; I swallowed it very willingly, offering it to the dear Eternal Father in atonement for the sufferings of his divine Son.

Farewell. Believe me your poor Mother Rosa, now and always, for all ages. Amen.”

She felt great sorrow and regret for the offense to the Lord and for the Daughter who had failed. She could not approve an error; but she did not condemn the Daughter. For the offense she suffered she had only words of sorrow: “I felt myself shudder…”, “a pill of wormwood…” She felt the feelings of Christ. Like Christ, she offered love. It was a love that forgives; a mother’s love wounded by “a pill of wormwood,” but which answered with the gentleness of forgiveness and with a commitment to a stronger mutual love. To another Daughter she said:

“You ask my forgiveness; I forgive you not once but a hundred times. And if the Superior reproves you, she does it for your good, for nothing else. But I always hold you close in the Heart of Jesus and pray much for you; if you improve your conduct, you will certainly receive God’s grace.”174

Looking at the Mother’s good example, the Daughters felt urged to follow her; they trusted her completely as a sure guide and teacher of holiness. In February 1867 Caterina Rapallino, one of Mother Rosa’s first followers, sent her this message:

“God has given you to me as a help and a guide to show me the way to heaven, to free me from the illusion in which I was living, to unite me more closely to you.”

Rosa’s words answered the most serious questions; they clarified the awareness of one’s vocation, enriched by the great abundance of her wise love. In the beginning the new Family offered no guarantee of stability. This might have led some parents to doubt its future. But the Daughters believed that everything would be easy, because their guide was a wise guide, who led them as on eagles’ wings; she saw from above the future of the Family and the events that shaped its present, in an essential and objective way. Her mere presence inspired trust, order, good government and harmony among all the Sisters. Her absence created a vacuum of authority and other problems. The Foundress did not let herself be overwhelmed by passing events. She was called to the intimacy of a willing “review,” to works of charity and to the “propagation of the faith.”

In 1866 she founded and organized the first community in Piacenza. In February 1867 she went to Cento (Ferrara) with eight postulants to found a second community at the hospital of that city. The Daughters in Piacenza awaited her every day. Wishing her to be with them, they wondered why she was so late.

The “wise” Mother does not feed on milk and honey. She wanted her Sisters solid, secure, authentic and free. On 18 February 1867 she sent them her answer:

“You told me that you were expecting me every day. My dears, how could that be, when in so few days one does not even know where the broth ladle is? So let us not deceive ourselves: in the works of the Lord, patience and sacrifice are needed. God likes sacrifices more than great promises and anything else. Jesus sacrificed himself for us and drank the bitter cup to the last evening, and we make so much trouble of being nearer rather than far. Ah! Come, my little ones, let us pull off our swaddling clothes ourselves (they are used for babies who cannot walk alone) and cast ourselves into the bosom of the Eternal One and beg him to do with us what he wills.”

The Daughters’ message, however, touched her deeply. How could she not understand their worries? She tried to console them with gentle and persuasive words. On 20 February 1867 she wrote to Giovanna Bixio:

“…Giovanna, my dear girl, come, courage, do not distress me, because hearing that you feel so bad gives me great pain. I shall soon be able to come into your arms and you into mine; it will always be as the Lord wills.”

When she left Cento, her Daughters, left alone with the growing difficulties of daily life, repeated their cry for help to the Mother. Mother Rosa, caring, patient and understanding, offered not only words and gestures of consolation, but went back to help them.

“Stop weeping; on Sunday without fail I will be in your arms… I tell you nothing more, because time does not allow it.”

She hastened to give them advice; she gave hope for the time of waiting. And she said to them:

“Believe me your Mother, who blesses you and clasps you to her bosom never to leave you again and to call herself always yours.”175

In another message she wrote:

“I assure you that I feel I am dying of desire to come, to be with you, to share in your charity. Yes, soon, I hope, and it is this alone that makes me work night and day so that I may fly to those I love so much, these sick people and you, my dear daughters.”176

“Yesterday I received your dear letters: I assure you they were a true consolation and made me laugh, and I needed to laugh… I will come to you as soon as I can… Yesterday, as soon as I received your letter, I sent you by the twelve o’clock coach a sack of potatoes and a basket of pears. I want you others to eat this fruit, without giving any away.”177

The Daughters’ “requests” strengthened the Mother’s compassion and mercy; benevolence and tenderness grew stronger in her heart. She answers Sr. Vincenza Rapallino’s questions thus:

“It is true that we are separated, but what do you want? Do you think I am made of marble and do not feel it? But if we think of doing everything for Jesus, I say that everything vanishes, and we always find ourselves united. You tell me that it seemed to you I was near. Yes, my dear, in spirit I am always with you and you can live in security. Cheer up, my dear, for the One we serve is a good Father, a most faithful Spouse, incapable of being unfaithful to us; we must not fear.”178

As the number of Daughters increased, Mother Rosa’s gift of love widened, opening to the immense dimensions of the “Being of her life,” of the reality of following Jesus, “holding the Cross tight to her breast.” On 29 October 1873 she sent this message to Sr. Paola Bucciotti:

“Today I received your letter and I hear how grieved you are, and I feel very great sorrow. I wish I could take them all from you and make them mine, that I might put them together with the others. I hear of sick Sisters, and I am most grieved. All for the Lord. See, my dear, this is the true road to go to Paradise and be near our God. Dear daughter, for Jesus everything is little. Come, courage, do not let yourself be cast down; reflect that we are on the cross, because we have embraced the cross as our inheritance. We do what we can on our part and the rest we must place in God.”

The love that the Daughters felt for her, even when expressed in “deeds,” was “proved” in the love of God and was confirmed with the strength and fidelity that mean remaining with Christ on the Cross. This was the pedagogical method by which Rosa Gattorno established her relationships with the Daughters. She expressed it in many different ways and never ceased to repeat it.

“You have told me many times, and with deeds you have shown me your love for me, for which I am exceedingly obliged to you, but how happy I would be if you confirmed it to me by giving me proofs that you love God very much and feel a great love for him; I assure you that this contentment would be of great relief to my oppressions. Come, then, come with me to Calvary for love of our Crucified, to be for him alone and together with him on the Cross!”179

4.3 In the community-family of the Holy Mother of Mary

The new religious Family that the Father had inspired in the field of the Church was part of his plan of salvation: to unite all humanity in a single family, gathered in the name of Christ. This community was a distinctive sign in the Church, because it lived steadily a eucharistic and liturgical life offered to the Father in Christ through the Spirit and, in expectation of fulfillment, hastened the coming of Christ into the hearts of all brothers and sisters, in a spirit of charity. Its distinctive sign was the charity that united all in “one heart.” From the beginning the Foundress clearly expressed the traits of the Family: “One heart and one thought, one aspiration, at the Center, to serve God.” The wonderful unity of “a hundred persons acting as one person” was a gift of God. The Daughters will always bless that “most holy Hand that with so much benevolence and charity keeps them united as one family.”180 They will develop gratitude and love for the Family that makes them grow spiritually as Daughters of St. Anne:

“I desire that they remember where they were born spiritually and that the Family is their true home, and that all direct their love to the Family.”181

As an experienced mother of a family, Rosa had the wisdom to create the supporting structures so that the environment of the community might develop a joyful, orderly and harmonious family atmosphere. First of all she prepared a chapel.

“Now that the Chapel is erected, we can say that we have a House of the Daughters of St. Anne.”182

“At this moment I am in Genoa and I take this minute to write to you so that you may have time to do what I would like to find prepared. Not only the guest room in order and clean, but also the whole house, especially the kitchen, which is always so dirty; have it whitewashed; the copper pots well cleaned, all hung in the first kitchen, the coffeepots too, in short that it be in order. The one at S. P. d’Arena looks like a drawing room, so bright and clean is it. The other day I took a friend of mine there who had arrived unexpectedly, and she said: ‘What fine cleanliness, not even in private houses is it kept like this.’ I understand that this one is all marble, and so the kitchen itself shines like a mirror, now that there is a tap with water that comes with force! […] Let us hope that the Lord will send us everything, all him, all, and to us the confusion and the humiliation.”183

Knowledge of the community’s positive progress consoled Mother Rosa.

“I have been to visit the two houses of S. P. d’Arena and Genoa; I can tell you nothing else than that I found an order, a harmony that truly gives consolation to find in those communities; so here at the main house and at the house of Death I can say nothing that afflicts me, but all goes very well. You more than all must give good example, because you were the new one of the new foundation and because you are so well protected by providence.”184

In the family atmosphere of joy and harmony, the Daughters of St. Anne are summoned to believe in the Spirit of Jesus Christ and to live the traits of the first Christian community.

“Pray and love one another with the same love, and take care to reach that beautiful unity of thinking and acting, so that all together you form one heart, one thought, because you all tend to one center, who is God.”185

A love with these characteristics positively opens space, among the sisters, for the mutual gift of friendship, in the common convergence toward one’s inner Center, in the decisive encounter with God and toward the same goal. The personal growth of each sister is considered a gift for the others in the community and a commitment to active service of charity. Helping one another in understanding and forgiveness. Entering the process of conversion to newness of life, which becomes a true gift and clear witness: “see how they love one another.” Spectacular gestures are not needed to show it. Life itself speaks and proclaims cohesion and mutual love through simple gestures, through a climate founded on reciprocal love.

Mother Rosa developed the community unity of the Daughters by stressing the importance of simple gestures. With a mother’s understanding and perception, she gave each one a fullness of affection and a joy of welcome, opening the person to a dimension of fraternal love, in a common gift of attention and love. Here is a passage from one of her letters:

“I will probably send you Sr. A. M. Vincenza to accompany the others. See that you show her all the attention she deserves, since she is still a child, so that you will not be divided, and do everything for St. Anne, Mother of the Immaculate. Let yourself be helped and rest, for I am sending her expressly for this.”186

The Sister entrusted to the other’s care was young not in age, being the same age as Sr. Francesca, but in religious life: she had received the habit of the Daughters of St. Anne only thirteen days before this letter.

A similar principle held for Adelaide Pezzoni, of delicate health, who needed, more than suitable and healthy food, a mother’s love and understanding. Mother Rosa entrusted her to the superior of the community in Ferrara, Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini:

“Just one line to tell you that I hear the teacher is better in health, so you will have her eat fatty foods. She loves you very much, and only wishes to know whether you are pleased, whether you love her and whether her conduct gives you satisfaction. Believe me, daughter, this sister of yours is very fond of you and desires nothing else than to satisfy you in all your wishes. God be blessed! What consolation I feel when I hear that peace reigns among you. May God keep it for you, for, poor creature that I am, every day I pray the good God to give it to you.”187

Fraternal charity, which according to a saying of Mother Rosa unites all in one heart, is a gift of God. This gift grows through prayer, drawing from the source of divine grace, and is expressed in the reality of the gift of self, every day, in a process of unifying diversities into a single unity.

“One heart,” “one thought” is set in the context of a community that is a reflection and anticipation of the Trinitarian dimension of community life. This gift is “already” present in the mystery of Christ’s presence; he is the Father’s gift, he reveals to us and helps us to love in every person of the community “the sister.” He makes us understand that only by grace are we called to be part of the Family of St. Anne, a refuge of peace, happiness, joy, welcome and forgiveness.

But this is “not yet.” The natural weakness and smallness of the persons called to follow this ideal create limits and barriers to the flow of love. Selfishness is always at work to hinder unity of purpose. Mother Rosa was its constant guardian; she did everything so that every community might be a Family of the Holy Spirit and live according to its spirituality. She often exhorts, clearly indicating the attitudes, methods and means needed to develop and strengthen fraternal communion in fidelity to the holy Rules. In an address to a group of nursing Sisters, Mother Rosa strongly condemned the lack of fraternal charity:

“Tell me, where is the charity that Jesus teaches us, who is the living example of charity? We must imitate him by never observing the faults of our fellow Sisters; if someone has erred, it was through distraction.”

Her zeal, her labor in continually seeking to help the Family of the Holy Mother in the communities, are attested by a letter written in Naples to a community whose name and location are unknown.

The beautiful letter speaks for itself. In it shines the passion of St. Paul to end the divisions among the Christians of Corinth and the bitterness of her motherly heart, deeply wounded by the Daughters’ wrong behavior:

“My daughters, I would like to say two words that in the name of the Lord might be engraved in your hearts; and I do not know where to find them better than in the Most Holy Heart of that love, Jesus. Daughters! Have pity and listen to me, it is a Mother who speaks to you, these are words of that most sweet Heart which through this miserable and unworthy Mother of yours comes to make you hear them.

By the first word he exhorts you to listen to him, the fountain of love; he calls you by the name of peace, which shows a lively desire that it return in you and that you all love one another in one way, held close in the one person of your Superior.

May peace be with you, and in you may the Spirit of charity be revived; let the wicked, or rather the monster, of murmuring be trampled. Oh!!! whispering! Diabolical spirit, I curse you!

I command you to leave what does not belong to you, which is my dearest Community: these are my daughters; the Blood of a God drew them from the claws of a corrupt world and under his standard placed them to fight under his flag;

and, abhorred by the Daughters of Zion, flee, for I curse you.

My daughters, alas! This name brings tears to my eyes at the thought that among you there is the seed of the weeds.

You, blessed of the Lord, who know well that you possess it, tear it from your heart and bring to the feet of the Lord the triumph of victory, your heart free of so foul a monster.

Ah, promise me to change your life, return from the mire to purity, and let your thought be one with mine, to be consumed for Jesus.

Be my comfort in these moments of toil and sacrifice with a letter from you in which you assure me that you will put into practice what I tell you, while I clasp you all in the most sweet Heart of my Jesus, and I tell you that I am torn by sorrow thinking of you. Have pity on me and tell me that you will reform your hearts, that on my coming I shall find you as I desire, all Love, where I hope to see you consumed in Jesus,

your most sorrowful Mother Sr. A. Rosa Gattorno.”

The strong reproofs condemn the evil in the community and denounce its source. But the strength of the spirituality and of the maternal feelings in which they are expressed is the pedagogy of a living teaching of forgiveness. It is also an outpouring of compassion, with the same measure as the heart of Christ toward the creatures of his Heart. It is a word of trust. Rosa Gattorno was not pessimistic with her Daughters. As a Mother, she believes deeply in them. Therefore, except in particular cases, she gives them joy and optimism by showing the ideal image of the community of communion that they are building; she outlines its essential reference points:

“Among themselves they will love one another with one heart and will always mirror themselves in their Spouse Jesus to look in him at the model to which they must conform; that is, to practice that evangelical charity of our Redeemer and the dear and holy humility.”

She gave this precise orientation, as the fundamental and primary teaching, to the first group of Daughters, the community of Cento, whose superior was Sr. Francesca Camisa, in July 1867, a few months after the foundation. In the same letter, after expressing the demands and purposes of the vocation, she reaffirmed the originality of the Institute’s spirit; she said that the Daughters must remember:

“Remember often to imitate the charity of your Mother St. Anne… to love one another with one heart, your Superior as Jesus, because you must see her in the figure of your Spouse. So imagine, if he commanded you, what obedience would you not give?”

The Daughters of St. Anne live according to the demands of fraternal charity in fidelity to their vows and direct their life, their talents and their service of charity through the mediation of the superior.

Mother and teacher of holiness

In a few years, from 1866 to 1872, Rosa Gattorno founded six communities, served by a considerable number of Sisters. From the very beginning of the new religious Order her life was total dedication. She was always animated by a missionary spirit of itinerancy:

“Continually on the road, now for some new community, now to seek money, so as to be able to help the Sisters financially.”188

In such extraordinary activity she put into practice what she contemplated; she prayed and fulfilled God’s plan by doing his work. From God she received light and strength to know and carry out his will in the development of the new religious Family that she was to serve through the Daughters of St. Anne, her Daughters. In order to fulfill that love toward God and toward brothers and sisters:

“My Jesus, no other motive leads us to lead this life than your love.”189

To build up the community of St. Anne within God’s plan means to form each Daughter as a living stone, who draws from Christ strength, maturity and stability; to nourish all her radical possibilities; to let herself be built up together with her Daughters by Christ. To make visible the Father’s maternal tenderness, become mercy toward all his creatures. This building up is therefore a divine work. She is only the poor and humble instrument of God’s will. She received herself from the Father as a free gift and offered herself to her Daughters. Her words are light, fire and life, and challenge the Daughters to imitate her positive example,190 because they are words she receives from her crucified Good. When she has to speak to the Daughters of St. Anne she assumes an attitude of deep listening:

“My Good, the ignorant one, your servant, must speak and treat of perfection. You, my Beloved Master, suggest to me and I will repeat… He seems to draw near to me, to dictate to me, many times; things of Sacred Scripture he suggests to me that I would never have known, other most beautiful ones he puts into my mind to say. Many times I too savor what I say, other times not: I speak as if in the third person and understand nothing of what I say and what I have said. In the end, what mercy! He sees the need of these creatures and speaks through the mouth of a donkey.”191

Her words expressed a real experience of communication with God, and were confirmed by the witness of her good example in daily life, in the humblest circumstances as in the most difficult events, in a climate of family relationships marked by great trust, cordiality and simplicity. Rosa Gattorno’s pedagogy is experiential. Her work of forming the Daughters of St. Anne is not founded on a systematic spiritual doctrine. The pedagogy arises from her life, which was an exodus that reached its goal. A pedagogy that develops from a personal reality marked by motherhood, which had profoundly shaped her being and her acting. And she devoted her life, to the fullest extent she could reach, to the intimate warmth of vital human relationships.

4.4.1. The following of Christ, way of love in poverty, chastity and obedience

“Come with me to Calvary.” On Calvary Christ’s dedication to the Father is revealed in fullness, in the ultimate gift of himself in sacrifice out of love; there is the boundless love of the Father, concentrated in mercy and goodness, a love that takes on in the Son the poverty of the children whom the Father calls to follow him, offering everyone his redeeming love. Calvary is for Mother Rosa the safe place of a redeeming rest, of fulfillment. Mother Rosa led her Daughters to Calvary starting from the opposite point of the mystery of Christ: the Incarnation. Exhorting them to adore and contemplate the mystery of Christ, she guides them on this path: to be with Christ in following him until becoming one; to follow Christ by dedicating oneself to the service and gift of charity toward brothers and sisters; to be with him in a vital and intimate communion; to seek him, because he loves us and wants us first. He himself makes himself small, within the reach of our stature, to encourage us with his love:

“A God who has made himself small and is nourished at a Mother’s breasts” (how much tenderness of maternal memories in this image!).192

“My dear, as the day of the great ineffable mystery of love approaches (Christmas), and everything gives us the means to feel, savor and learn to love and be nourished by this most living love, this delightful pledge that comes to us to teach us the way by which we must go to draw this tasty milk: behold, a God as he was has made himself small and is nourished at a Mother’s breasts, having lowered his power by his pure love, reducing himself to the most humble and poor child…

And you, King of heaven and earth, with nothing but a handful of straw and a few linens to wrap you, for fire in so horrible a cold season you knew only the warmth of the breath of two beasts. Here, my dear, look at how many points of meditation and consideration there are in the way our Good came to trace: first, he left everything. So, if you want to find me, he says, you must leave every affection, love and complacency, and drown yourself only in a sea that can satisfy all your desires, a fountain that will quench your thirst, however great your ardor. Rich, because the riches I can give you you can never possess,

however powerful you may be on this earth of mud and misery. But look at him: he has no clothes, so to go to him and have the riches from him it is necessary to be stripped, poor and naked, so he will clothe us in beautiful garments adorned with precious gems.

My dear, it is true that all these things are very distasteful to our humanity, because it feels itself stripped of its sensual tastes and reduced to the nothingness of its sensible feeling; but what a consolation it would be for me when you hold yourselves annihilated in everything and seek only to please your Spouse Jesus.

So, my daughter, ah! courage to fight well against the sad powers of sense and flesh and to will at all costs that our spirit be always victorious in us and to seek to correspond to every inspiration that our Jesus continually does not cease to give us and many times makes us feel strongly, and we, with the greatest indifference, reject them as if they were nothing; yet of these one day a great account will be asked of us. Woe to the creature who has made herself deaf to the inspirations that God, in his mercy, gives her!”

“If instead we listen to him and if we always act for him alone, he takes such pleasure in us that he is enchanted. Oh! blessed the soul that manages to enchant the Beloved, the eternal Being of all souls, the Eternal Father who knows all: two spouses in love with each other. They have no other thought than to try to do everything the beloved desires. The bride will please beloved Jesus by doing everything for him and welcoming every cross, trying to relieve him of the weight of the crosses that the wicked have placed on his shoulders. And what will this sovereign Spouse do for his beloved! What precious gems of great value will these gifts be! What wonderful, sweet and gracious gifts!”193

In tracing for her Daughters the way of perfection, Mother Rosa, as we have already observed, is precise and demanding, but also understanding.

She has welcomed the Lord into her heart; she creates enough space for a serene and warm welcome of the Daughters and involves them in living the gift with greater determination and fullness. Mother Rosa sent this advice to Sr. Giovanna Bixio, one of her first five companions in Piacenza:

“Call on Jesus when you are flustered and you will see that he will console you. Go to the foot of the altar and say this: I intend to unite myself in prayer with my Mother Rosa, and ask him what you desire. If you were physically ill, ask him for bodily health; if spiritually, tell him that you want to love him and humbly beg him to come into your heart to bring it peace and union with God, love of neighbor, charity and obedience to Superiors, and that at the cost of your life you want to be his faithful and loving bride and wish to become a perfect religious… you want to obey blindly… bear all annoyances… sympathize with everyone… keep your thought always in God and see everything with his eye… do with dedication everything that is commanded us.”194

In these letters of spiritual direction by Mother Rosa the main element is always the love of God. To welcome this love is to let oneself be guided like children, to trust him in everything. The Daughters seek in the reality of daily life the expression of his will in order to follow it, please him and be his joy. To do God’s will and to obey is the surest proof of love and the most tangible fulfillment of the following of Christ, who became a Servant, obedient unto death on the Cross. If we want to walk with Jesus, we must act as Jesus did.

Love expressed in obedience is the surest way to make us saints, to lead us to the summit of Mount Carmel and to the love that identifies itself with the Crucified, in sharing in the paschal mystery of Christ.

Mother Rosa expressed her thought thus in an instruction to the community of Sampierdarena on 7 April 1872. She observes that not all the sisters are strong and courageous in following the Christian way, in practicing the virtue of humility and that of obedience; not all follow Christ closely on the way of obedience and love.

There are three ways of following the Christian path; three roads that can lead to different results. The first road is full of tribulations, thorns, hedges, failures, humiliations and denial of one’s own will. It leads to acquiring the spirit of Jesus, humility, meekness, obedience and total abandonment to the supreme Lord. The second road is less difficult to travel; this too has obstacles along the way, but streams of water refresh the soul and flowers bloom along the path. It leads to humility, meekness and a lessening of one’s own will. The third road is pleasant, wide, without obstacles, roses bloom there and even the thorns of the roses are sweet: it is the road traveled by lukewarm virgins who do not want to prick themselves too much.

The conditions for following Jesus

The way of love is not easy to travel. To walk swiftly without losing one’s bearings, one must fight effectively and will that the spirit be always victorious at all costs. It is clear that it is a way of ascent with precise conditions. First of all humility: one must look honestly at one’s own life, the world, God, and live without superficiality with courageous determination, letting oneself be guided by God with absolute trust:

“Keep yourselves humble, for this is the only way not to fall and to become saints.”195

“Let us think, my daughters, that in these days (of Lent) we have the model of the holy humility practiced by Jesus, and the Church keeps us occupied in these days teaching us the way to imitate this model of every virtue, beginning with the going to the Jordan. What a lowering! The most perfect, the purest God-Man wished to submit to being on a par with the sinner, purified with the water of holy baptism in the Jordan, but Heaven opened, and a voice that could not contain itself said: ‘This is my Son…’ Jesus, what are you doing?… enough; but no: to greater torments he goes to subject his delicate humanity!”196

The way of love toward the one Center who is God requires decision and resolution: God alone is the priority. This aim demands overcoming every uncertainty, laziness, hesitation, conquering the internal difficulties of human nature and also the external ones. So that the Daughters may effectively follow the Christian way, the Mother enrolls them as pupils in the school of Jesus: to become apprentices of this art requires a fundamental commitment, a daily dedication in the ascent, made of vigilance, of acceptance of the difficulties of each day; it means dying spiritually to worldly concerns, it is sacrifice, it is solitude. In a word it is the Cross of Jesus, the treasure that the world does not know. To be marked with the sign of Jesus means to live every day with fidelity the love of Jesus: the sisters must make themselves small to run toward Jesus. They must beg him to “make them beautiful.” In this awareness lies our strength, our courage; it sustains our fidelity.

“Yes, dear ones of Jesus, courage and firm constancy and you will see with this God’s help… Let us run to the Master, to learn everything and with the simplicity of children… Look at Peter. Come! the Master said to him, and he, without thinking that he had a family and other things, ran at once.

So it was for all those who followed the Savior. Certainly this Master did not go out for walks and pleasures, but was ready for everything, paying no attention either to food or to clothing, in search of the lost sheep. Together all these Apostles went with Jesus to suffer hunger and thirst. Behold, whoever wishes to follow me, says the Master (showing us a cross), let him take up his cross and follow me.

So, what language is this? Heavenly Spouse! O blessed souls! He gives me that treasure which the world does not know and which he offers to his beloved Brides… But since this treasure is also burdensome at the beginning, it is enough never to stop, even at the cost of having to drag it along; it is then that Jesus helps us to carry it…

And then not only does the cross fall, but we too follow it. But what must we do then? Courage! All dejected, because wrapped in our littleness we see ourselves ragged on all sides, trembling, we no longer know how to call the Spouse, because he is all beautiful and we are deformed.

What to do? Let us humble ourselves and, crying out, call him to our help as Father of pity and love, and with words full of compunction let us beg him, as children do, to pull us up and make us beautiful, so that we do not become deformed and driven away by the Spouse. Ah! How this love is pleased to see himself treated in this way! Not as certain souls do, who think him a tyrant. If he permits it, it is to humble us still more and make us pleasing in the eyes of his Father.”197

She wishes her Daughters to be perfect imitators of Christ, in garments enameled and adorned with his Blood, because Jesus wants them wholly his, wants to grow in them:

“Giving us his food and strengthening us with the precious wine of his Blood. On this he wants us to live in this life, and then to come into his presence in the purple robe enameled with his most divine Blood. This purple we cannot have unless we climb the Cross; […] the nuptial bed of his most beloved brides.”198

She sent this message to Sr. Francesca Camisa:

“My daughter, God wants you on a road that he usually takes his beloved on, it is dark, full of thorns, pains, but do you know what he does when they find themselves at the end of it? He intoxicates them with his delicious wine, so that they forget themselves and, in suffering, run thirsty along this road;

they feel the thorns, but the pricks are sweet to them; they feel the torments of their breast and these are changed for them into palpitations of love, because they feel nothing more, hear nothing more than a fiery blaze of love that drags them to seek the beloved, and, if to reach him it were necessary to descend into the abyss of hell, they would descend there into those atrocious pains, having finally found their Good. Not even there would they feel anguish, because this Being sweetens everything, and is that nectar that lies within the sharpest thorns.”199

4.4.2. The law of love: the Cross

In the documents quoted here the spiritual path traveled by Rosa Gattorno clearly appears. She reached transforming union with her “crucified Good.” In her teaching, while taking into account the objective reality of the Daughters, there can be no separation from the spiritual fervor of her mystical experience. From the intense union with God the Trinity springs the irresistible force of the charism of her motherhood: as life to be given. Her life is Christ, her Good. His love has conquered her:

“My Jesus, Heart of Jesus, Love of Jesus, Hope of Jesus, tongue of Jesus… Jesus for me… I live for him!”200

She speaks only of Jesus, who is everything in her life.

“I would like to tell you and speak to you of this dear Love… My daughter, love, for charity’s sake; and keep all your love for this Being without reserve: all for him, yes, all!”201

Of this dear Love she has discovered the mysterious and terrible choice: the Cross. The Cross is the only way of holiness, the most sublime way; and her Daughters must not fear the sufferings of the Cross. She begs her Good that her Daughters embrace the Cross and that his nectar inebriate them, purifying suffering through love. To be with Jesus one must accept, like Jesus, the Cross of Redemption.

“Oh! if my dear Crucified grants my request, the love of God will surely consume you. Love! Love! It is your only help in all your sorrows and tribulations, and live only for him. May God help you to become as I desire you.”202

She shared in the Cross with growing intensity. Every day there is a flood of crosses. And the irresistible force of love grows richer. And she goes toward her Daughters and toward everyone in the dynamism of a vital mission, with the richness of the natural gifts of femininity, which blossoms in a motherhood sublimated in the spirit.

Mother Rosa proclaims the wonders of God as Mary did, the first Daughter of St. Anne. She wishes to proclaim to all in a loud voice that in love lies the only good. The empty and free heart is inhabited by the Being who:

“makes us too, poor creatures, God’s; or better, God in the creature, we remain one single thing with the Creator.”203

Creatures become an emptiness in which Christ offers the gifts of the Holy Spirit:

“Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.”204

To welcome the gift of the Spirit is the intimacy of a life of continual prayer that involves everything, soul, body and spirit, and becomes desire, aspiration to be for Jesus, with Jesus and in Jesus:

“To live for him, to die for him… A short suffering for an eternal enjoyment.”

4.4.3. The demands of love

As an expert spiritual teacher, the Mother does not limit herself to showing her Daughters the joys of true holiness. One arrives at the summit of Calvary, the culmination of love and spousal gift, by passing through the stations of the Way of the Cross. To travel the road effectively without deviating, without getting lost, discouraged or afraid, the right means are needed. Mother Rosa illustrates them with a Mother’s tenderness, drawing them not from the reading of ascetical books but from her own life. This gives them effectiveness, power of conviction and relevance.

Concentrating the heart on God

“We must have one object only that occupies our thought, our heart; the one object of our life is God alone. We must live for him, be crucified for him. Daughter, what use is the whole world if we do not have God? None, and less than none.”205

“Dear Daughter, love Jesus and hold him always close to your heart; from time to time, during the day, bow your head a little toward your heart, and say to Jesus who is hidden within: ‘My Love, make me wholly yours, and be wholly mine, dear Jesus.’ Another time you can say to him: ‘My Beloved, what are you doing in here, alone, in so small a dwelling? Ah! speak to me, and quiet my doubts, confirm me in your love. Jesus, my Redeemer, give me your love!’”206

To live in spousal intimacy, to believe in love, to let oneself be guided by love, always to seek the one object of our life. Mother Rosa guides her Daughters toward the summit. There every Daughter must seek to be truly a perfect religious, in fidelity to all the means that the Family of the Holy Mother offers. The principal means are: prayer and silence, observance of the Rule and sacrifice.

“Remind yourselves often why you became Religious: to become saints and to acquire little by little the love of God… to this divine love you must come.”207

Prayer and silence

It is important to pray, to pray always. One must fill life with prayer, speaking continually with the Lord, seeking him in one’s own heart and in brothers and sisters.

“Courage, my dears, pray much; laugh little; pray much and meditate a great deal, because you always have a way to meditate by seeing Jesus in the sick, and therefore the meditation on the Passion of Jesus will come easily to you.”208

“Prayers make our life fruitful in good works, enrich our actions and our good deeds, attract the Lord’s pleasure and the wonderful joy of being loved by God.”209

Prayer is spiritual wealth.

“Prayer is the key of graces: it opens the Lord’s treasure.”210

“I have no other treasure than prayer; from it I have everything, and with it I obtain all the courage and hope that one day we shall find our labors at the Throne of God the Judge, and that they will defend us from falling into the abyss as we deserve.”211

Prayer is the center of Christian life.

“Take care, my Daughters: in joys, in sorrows, in tribulations, in your good works, always lean on prayer.”212

“Daughter, if you are sad, run to church and pour out your heart to Jesus, weep with him and then, when you have dried your tears, back to work again, all to all, and full of sweet emotion, to pass it on to others.”213

To pray is to listen to the Beloved.

“If we all worked on our little plot of land that God has given us to cultivate, and formed in our heart a solitary dwelling, and thought of nothing else but loving and serving good God!… and in the solitude of this inner room made an altar to adore our one Jesus!… Oh, then all other things could not come to wound our ear, but instead we would always be intent on listening to his voice, which can be heard in solitude. Blessed are you, Daughters, who from work can pass to the inner room in retreat.”214

In living the virtues of the Family of the Holy Mother in this climate of uninterrupted and faithful prayer, in the search for and discernment of what pleases the Father, the true identity of the Daughters of St. Anne is formed.

The Rule of 1869 expressed the dynamism articulated in the seven typical virtues of the Family of the Holy Mother: faith, hope, charity, simplicity and prudence, humility and meekness.

Mother Rosa recognized in the Rule of 1869 the authentic interpretation of the charism and considered it a code of life for herself and for her Daughters; she wanted the Rule to be learned and faithfully observed by the Daughters.

“Try to imprint them on your heart and mind in order to observe them exactly.”215

In the Rule lies the treasure, the patrimony, the solid foundation on which the Daughter of St. Anne is built up according to the spirit and becomes the beloved of God.

“…For these, who are truly the consolation of the holy Mother, I feel a great affection, and I look at them with pleasure, as my Mother St. Anne looks at them!”216

Faith, hope and charity, as three dimensions of living in communion with God that every Christian must have, are lived by the Daughters of St. Anne in the original spirit of the founding charism. They are gifts for a mission.

These gifts make the Daughters a living temple of the heart, a true land of Christ, from the roots of their femininity; their destiny is to share in the motherhood of God.

“My daughter… You need a strong faith to believe that you are united with God and are helping him, so to speak, in the greatest work he accomplishes in this world, that is, in helping people in body and spirit, so that they may become blessed in heaven; and that he gives you in this task his Holy Spirit, his Providence, his mercy with which he helps people.”

“Make yourself firmly persuaded that, when you are well planted in this heavenly hope, you will always live as a child in the arms of your heavenly Father… Faith and hope aspire to charity, which is like the soul and life of the two of them… My daughter, Charity inflamed with pure love of God was truly that heavenly fire that made my womb fruitful, so that I might worthily conceive with an immaculate conception my daughter Mary… This Jesus Christ taught us with those words of his which say: The things that please my Father I always do.”217

The Mother integrates these “sublime teachings,” as she herself calls them, into daily life with strong human and spiritual energy, the fruit of a living understanding of spiritual things and of insight into God’s way of thinking. She advises Sr. Francesca Camisa:

“Be at peace again and think that this poor mother of yours always holds you close to her, because she desires that the Holy Mother make you a saint. She says to the Eternal Father: ‘Make of this creature a true dough of your will, that in everything she may feel pleasure in serving you, our Father, our support, our guide.’”218

To another Sister, Sr. Adelaide Pezzoni, she wrote:

“Let us bless the Lord, our help, our teacher, who knows so well how to teach us, and let us see to profiting by his lessons and being studious in order to please him and fully satisfy his will. My daughter, if you knew what consolation I feel merely in pronouncing these words, to please God, and still more if the sweet thought of being or being able to become his pleasure awakens vividly in me, I feel quite beside myself, so that if I had to face the cruelest martyrdom I would feel nothing.”219

“Daughter, courage and patience, you will see that soon the Lord will come with special providence… I do not lack, even in the slightest, trust in God the Father. Let us pray fervently, so that our prayers may reach the loving heart of Jesus; it is there that the source of all spiritual and temporal wealth is found. Take care of the observance of the holy Rules, another most powerful means of having the right hand of the Eternal Father favorable.

Dear hand, which wherever it turns its gentle finger heals every wound of ours. Daughter, love this dear Eternal Father, and make your daughters love him, for if they love this God the Father, our one and only good, they will become perfect and will be able to do whatever they wish, for everything will be done well. A line to all: My blessed daughters, stand firm and all confidence in God. Hold close, love your privations… and with joy offer them to your Eternal Father, that he may deign to accept them and keep them, changing them into some little treasure of his. What delight, Daughters, to think that for so little suffering you will have a great joy, and your heart in anticipation will feel the joy of the love of its Beloved.”220

Rule of 1869:

Simplicity and prudence

“My daughter… in me was fulfilled the word of Jesus Christ, that God is pleased to reveal his secrets to the simple… For to me was revealed one of his most hidden counsels, I mean that of the Immaculate Conception of Mary… My daughter, in imitation of me, see that there is no duplicity in you: let everything in you be light… in all your actions look to nothing but your true treasure, which is the pleasure of your God, and then he will willingly converse intimately with you.

My daughter, simplicity cannot live without the company of prudence… Prudence is that light which, between two things, makes you always choose the one that better leads you to acquire and increase the only solid wealth, that is, the love of God… So it is with acting; always discern what is more for the glory of God and the benefit of his neighbor… My daughter, prudence was so much with me that it made me worthy to give birth to her who is the most prudent Virgin. Follow me, and so you will be simple as the dove and prudent as the serpent.”

Humility and meekness

“My daughter, you see me placed by God on the Throne of the highest dignity as Mother of his own divine mother… So it means that I was, after Mary, the most humble among creatures: humility being the road to the exaltation that comes from God… The humble person, my daughter, carries deeply engraved in her soul those words of Jesus Christ which say: Whoever among you wishes to be the greatest, let him become the least and the servant of all. Blessed are you if you inherit this virtue: you will always live in peace and joy.

Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the land… Human nature in the person of woman is that land which was created by God so that it might bring forth fruits of blessing for him… I alone among women obtained this blessing, because I alone from my womb brought forth her who alone was Immaculate; and so my flesh was truly holy land… And was not Mary herself the true land, new land, which from her flesh by the sole power of the Holy Spirit produced Jesus Christ, who is the fruit of the true knowledge of good and evil?… Now Mary was a wealth of mine; and if I deserved her from the Father of the family, it was because I offered him a meekness equaled by no meek person. Therefore you would not be my worthy daughter if you were not very distinguished in this virtue.”221

Mother Rosa says:

“May God bless you and may truth always remain on your lips, and simplicity in your heart.”222

“Jesus, beloved of frank and good souls, you who are truth and life, you who love those who bear truth on their lips, make my Carolina a true dove and your model in speaking.”223

To the same Sister:

“…This poor Mother of yours never forgets her little girl. Little girls are extremely dear to Jesus, but do you know what kind of little girls Jesus loves? Simple, humble ones who, being small, do not yet have that monster of self-love which is the property of the old man. The Virgin Mary, because she too is a lover of little doves, likes little girls and loves them very much, because in them pride and its sister vainglory have not yet grown.”224

“My daughter, every time you have to speak, never think with too much anxiety what you must answer, wanting to use your own wit; no, no, present yourself to anyone without study, only that of charity and gentleness, without affectation and with simplicity, always united to God, in his presence; and then speak without fear, for you will say everything well. Oh! sweet Jesus, whoever loves you knows how to speak well! So, Daughter, love, and then do what you will, and you will do everything well.”225

“Dearest Daughters, humility, the sure and only foundation for sanctifying ourselves; without it we can hope for nothing for eternal life. It is written: if you want to enter up there you must become small and humble. The Lord said to a soul: ‘Do not care for yourself, but only put your trust in me and you will have everything.’ So think of being all Jesus’, for Jesus always thinks of giving you what you need. Oh! blessed are you if he gives you his love!… this love certainly cannot be had without humility.”226

“As for the Daughters who have left, I believe they should be received back, because Jesus wants us to do so. How many are the sinners who fall and return to him and are received with mercy? Take them back, then, for I know that all our actions done against our evil will, but only for his Love, will always please God. Let us love him in our sisters and love them.”227

“Jesus is all patience and meekness; he is also charity and love. With these virtues our Holy Mother St. Anne was also adorned.”228

“I recommend to you, Daughter, meekness, because this is the true character of a ‘Daughter of St. Anne Mother of the Immaculate.’ If we are to imitate the Holy Mother, we must be so; otherwise we will never be recognized as daughters of so holy a Mother, and will remain among the reprobate.”229

“Peace, Daughters, peace, silence, calm; then you will hear God come to speak to your heart with loving and altogether sweet words.”230

“Believe me, my daughter, gentleness is a powerful weapon for winning hearts and leading them to love Jesus. It is also what keeps a good fragrance in a community, spreading its perfumes on those who approach us, and indeed I am of the opinion that we poor Daughters of St. Anne M. of the Immaculate more than all the others must be adorned with it, because, being continually in contact with outsiders, we must leave in them, every time we speak to them, very lively impressions of a taste for religion… How fine it is to see in the parlor that Religious whose modest bearing is accompanied by a gentleness and humility so sincere, nothing affected, nothing studied… It is easy for her to hide every displeasure and discomfort, but always in the presence of everyone she remains cheerful and content to show others that the religious spirit is a comfort and the true repose of our souls.”231

4.5 Mother, educator and superior of the Daughters

In her human motherhood Rosa Gattorno had staked all the richness of her being in the gift of life. In her spiritual motherhood, the great gift of her Good of love, her unconditional maternal dedication drew nourishment from the inexhaustible resources of the infinite Being; she felt God possessing her soul and proclaimed herself, like Mary, God’s most humble servant. It is a spiritual motherhood that is born of God for the Kingdom, to flower and bear good fruit in his Vineyard and in his Work. She served, developed and strengthened the life entrusted to her, fulfilling God’s plan. Her dedication is for all. Since she does not belong to herself but wholly to her Good, the richness of the gift of creation and salvation she received becomes the patrimony of her Daughters of St. Anne. Every Daughter, like Mother Rosa, is called to work generously for the Work of God, cultivating the little plot of land that God has given her to cultivate232 in the specific task entrusted to her by obedience; to each she gave all her love and attention, because in every Daughter she loved to see the profile of the true Daughter of St. Anne.

She gave very special care to the formation of the Superiors; to them she entrusted the most delicate task of guiding the sisters on the way of holiness, in fidelity to the spirit of the Institute. She worked tirelessly, offering herself as their guide so that they could carry out this task effectively. Her first followers were very young: almost all were about twenty.233

They shared Mother Rosa’s ideal; they knew how to live in harmony with the plan of the foundation, expressing the charism in concrete forms. From among them she chose the Superiors not by the criterion of age but by the discernment of the Spirit, sole giver and perfecter of all gifts. She cared for them like tender seedlings, with respect and delicacy. She saw their inexperience and the importance of the responsibility of a community. “My daughter Adelaide, so young and already mother of so many daughters.”234 She watched over them with optimism, encouraging them in moments of discouragement, so that they might stop looking at their own smallness and inability and concentrate on God, who was calling them to a great work.

The Daughters opened up to her; they confided doubts, worries and sorrows, asked her for advice and directives. The Mother gave each one the right answer, in person or promptly by letter. Sr. Adelaide Pezzoni, who had been directress and teacher in the community of Sampierdarena, now that she was superior in Piacenza, thought the task of educator suited her abilities better. Being a superior was a heavy burden. The Mother answered her with the usual counsels of love and spirituality:

“My daughter forever, reading your letter I could not find peace: how can Sr. Maria Adelaide have foolish thoughts? No, it is all the work of the devil. She is not yet expert in this career, she always lets herself be overcome by melancholy; let us unmask the liar. My daughter:

  1. look where you are, where God has placed you. Look at the vast and most beautiful garden of the Savior, of which he is the Gardener; look how he has raised you to sublime greatness, to be an active part of his new Order, born in the bosom of his beloved Spouse, of which one day we shall know the full extent, goodness and power, and whoever works in it gains eternal life. We shall see all this in the glory of the Blessed, where we must hope to go by God’s pure mercy. It is in Heaven that things are seen clearly and the fallacious reasonings of the world end.

  2. You would like to devote yourself to the education of girls. Well, what are we to say if the Lord wants you more wholly his, in a greater and more demanding condition? What do you want to do? Do you prefer the world, how horrible that would be!, or to submit to the service of an infinite Being, a Master who does not know how to command, because he loves us too much and his commands are all love? He makes himself Father to teach us, he makes himself Spouse to give us everything. You say you are useless. What? I say: are you then sorry to help your poor Mother carry the weight she has on her shoulders? What are these words of love, those eager wishes to relieve so many sorrows? So, my daughter, are they only superficial words? No, they are not. My Sr. Adelaide cannot be a hypocrite.”235

To the same person:

“…I would like my Delegate in these days to act truly as a mother, a wise, prudent, strong, constant mother, patient in carrying the heavy cross that her Jesus has placed on her shoulders. Ah! Daughter, if you try to carry this with patience and resignation, you will enter that beautiful Paradise which Jesus made expressly for Superiors who are to their community a mirror and model of virtue. Consider that all eyes are on you and, if they see holy works in you, will they not feel a desire to imitate you? And then, through you, all will become holy. And God will give you that fine place which will be of greater glory above all, and in the bliss of that sight, in seeing so many souls praise God through your cooperation, you will rejoice in rejoicing in God.”236

Mother Rosa is very firm in her certainty of being close to the infinite Being, whose commands are all love; she strengthens the Daughters’ hesitations. If Jesus puts the cross of the superior on their shoulders, he does not leave them to carry it with their own strength alone. She considers it a gift to be lived in docility and in listening to God’s teaching. The Holy Mother is near all her Daughters as a vigilant guide and tender Mother.

“Why are you so fearful about the post you have received? No, you must be at peace and full of trust in God. Speak with the Holy Mother: she is always with you to suggest what you must say and do. We are only saws in the smith’s hand237.

Courage and all love for Jesus and for the Holy Mother St. Anne.” “The Lord God and the tender Mother St. Anne will hold you by the hand, and the work of your gentle government will be blessed.”238

“Why, then, fear? Without God’s help we are capable of nothing, and with his help we have everything.”239

Letters like these reveal the strong character of such a Mother, her charm, her power of persuasion, her educational capacity, which develops qualities and attitudes in the Daughters, clarifies and strengthens their awareness of total belonging to God in his Work. She is close to the Superiors, not only in the early years of the Institute but always. Until a few months before her death she continued to write, restating the principles that inspire good government of communities. Some written testimonies, taken from the many letters to Superiors throughout her life, outline the image of the Superior seen with her heart and in the perspective of the charism.

“The Superiors of the houses must act as mothers to the Sisters, so that the Sisters, who have left their mothers and their families, may find in her a maternal affection that wins their full confidence.”240

“Superior, you must treat your Daughters with a mother’s love.”241 “Try to be a mother to these Sisters and these girls.”242

“The Superior is the one who, with good manners, can turn her Daughters away from every bad inclination and direct them on the right way of holiness and perfection, to have them with her in heaven for an eternity of joy.”243

The Superior must know how to educate the Sisters.

“Everything lies in knowing how to cultivate them. They are plants that, if they have no fertilizer, dry up, and we must try to water them with the healthful water of the kind that our Master Jesus spoke of to the Samaritan woman. So a Superior must try to do everything so that her sisters may have their fill of drinking such water; so, meditation well performed in church, the same prayers in church; and see to gathering them frequently and giving them fine exhortations.”244

The Superior is the expression of the living Rule.

“I recommend to you the observance of the Rule; you must be first in everything, so you will do very well, because you will be regularly firm in keeping prayer and meditation. Whoever does these well is sure to observe the rest.”245

“The Superior must be the lighthouse that guides all to the safe harbor.”

“For charity’s sake… observe the Rule… let the day of retreat be kept in silence and let the Rules be read, so that the sisters may learn them by heart and you may always be guided in everything by the holy words of our Rules; then providence will never fail you. Always pray well and with fervor.”246

“Patience, docility, resignation are the qualities that God requires a good Superior to have. Are you sorrowful? Run to Church and cry out with Jesus, weep, and then, when you have dried your tears, back to work again, all to all and full of sweet unction, to pass it on to others.”247

To her secretary, sent to a community to stay for a certain period to help and guide the local superior, she advised:

“See that you tell that Superior to be docile with the sisters and all heart and kindness, because the sisters are religious equal to her and we are all equal. For charity’s sake, take care that she does not mistreat them, but treats them with charity and love.”248

To the superior Sr. Paola Bucciotti she sent by post other precious counsels:

“We must show no preference in our dealings with the sisters, neither spiritual nor temporal, so that the sisters may imitate us not in the extraordinary, but in the exact observance of the Rules.”249

One becomes a model and center of fraternal unity by taking on the same sentiments as Jesus Christ. He renewed us in love and peace, taking away sin by his death, giving himself up to the extreme of self-abasement. Therefore the fundamental virtue of superiors is humility.

“Yes, my Daughter, think that humility is the base of every virtue and whoever has it possesses God. Yes, my Daughter, learn this beautiful practice and you will have everything from the Lord. Your house will be a gem in the eyes of my Crucified and you will be his Beloved. Courage then, for violence is needed to win the kingdom of Heaven.”250

The Superior who has the sentiments of Christ performs a service of love toward the sisters with the attitude of the Holy Mother, whose heart was full of mercy.

“Charity has no limits! Oh, love, you are the fruit of charity! What shall I say of your letter? If you live all charity, you will feel great sorrow for the young sister overburdened with work, who complains. Oh! poor humanity, what bitter fruits you produce! Therefore I have absolutely forbidden the teacher to hold school during the holidays. No, no, she absolutely needs to rest before beginning to teach again, because teaching is tiring work. So, if she is still holding school, let her stop at once and rest, and let the others rest too. All the teachers absolutely need rest. We understand each other, do we not? If the administrators have anything to say, let them write to me and I will answer them. Have you understood? Farewell, believe me yours for all eternity, your affectionate M. Rosa.”251

The Superior’s lesson was healthful:

“Live all charity. Charity has no limits, because it is measured by the measure of the Master, who gives himself to us as food.”252

“Be charitable and gentle with your fellow Sisters, if you want to win their hearts and become holy with them.”253

“Use much prudence, charity, humility and gentleness with everyone: with your sisters and with the other people you meet, and you will win the hearts of all to give them to the Lord.”254

The Superior, like a good mother of a family, is attentive, tireless, watchful and caring in everything, so that order, harmony and vigilance may reign.

“My dear, listen, for charity’s sake, I recommend order to you and that you watch that not the least of the least things of the good order that I left there be lost.”255

“Attention to everything: to the school, the looms, the kitchen; be all fire of concern, go round always to see that all the sisters do their duty. I recommend the looms to you, the cleanliness of the dormitories, that the little girls be clean. Do not forget to watch over the school and the wardrobe and the pantry.”256

The “fire of concern” is the solicitude of love that makes the Superior the guide and coordinator of everyone’s energies, so that one heart and one soul may give themselves tirelessly to the work of the Lord.

“First of all I recommend to you daily economy, which means being careful with the cent, which in time makes 100 francs. You will not believe it, and it is just your way, not knowing that it is from nothing, that is, from little, that one comes to much. You are still inexperienced in this particular and do not know this language, because you are young and not used to managing a house, but this poor Mother of yours, who is old and knows these things well, sees them and is displeased by them, because, living on providence, we must pay attention to everything, and then our holy Rules require it of us.”257

Living in trust in Providence, without fixed income, exposed them to uncertainty, anxiety and worry, above all where there were many persons to support. The Mother helps them to found the need of today and tomorrow not on uncertain human hopes and securities, but on God the Father.

“Let us trust in God, and he, since the Work is his, will provide for everything.”258

“I rejoice that God has sent you a little providence; let us thank our dear Treasurer. I would like to know whether you have paid the pharmacist and how much you owe the milkman, and the other accounts. Let us pray the Lord to send us providence and let us never lose heart; let us always trust in God’s mercy, let us not cease to do so.”259

On 29 April 1877 she wrote to a superior:

“You, because of the debts you have incurred, to meet them make economies that are too exaggerated, even taking the necessary from yourself and others; so drop at once so ugly a way of proceeding and begin to have meat and milk and wine bought, in the quantity and quality that a community of active persons such as you require. So I hope you will do this at once, and we shall pay the debts, do not doubt.”260

The Mother understood, intervened and freed all from every kind of fear. But she demanded faith in God:

“I sympathize with you, but I do not like dejection, because that belongs to worldly, wretched people who have no trust in their God, because they scarcely know him and do not love him at all.”261

“Courage, do not be anxious, God will do everything. Whoever lives for him is sure that he will defend him.”262

“Courage, go on, for Jesus will help you, so be strong and write to me. Ah! Yes! You will see that the Lord will send you providence and you will pay your accounts, and then, having no debts, you will be able to breathe and make some fine provision for the winter, such as potatoes and wine; it would suit you to take a little grape and make it at home. What do you say?”263

The Superior must have the temper of the strong woman and a spirit of sacrifice able to withstand every trial.

“Let us work, for then we shall rest blessed. Be strong, Daughter, do not fear; this poor mother of yours will always be at your side, wherever you go; see that you keep yourself in God’s presence and you will see that you will have everything.”264

“When I see what you do and that you act according to what God inspires you, I feel immense consolation. Courage: in difficult times one must be strong.”265

“Courage, Daughter, go forward without fear. Jesus wants generous souls. Always give me good news, for I assure you they are a true comfort to me. Oh! my God! Bless my dear Daughter, that she may become an exemplary Superior and that in her mirror many models be drawn such as your Work requires!”266

From trials and struggles one emerges strengthened and becomes aware of one’s responsibility as spiritual guide of the sisters and as manager of the economic and administrative affairs of the community. One becomes an effective instrument of God in his work, sustained not by one’s own merits but by the grace of the vocation in the Family of the Holy Mother of Mary Immaculate; one performs one’s role with maturity.

The Mother says it in different ways and at the opportune moments. She sent this message to Sr. Biagia Pedroni, who was worried about the economic affairs of the community:

“You say that I will approve your accounts. Listen, do you know what I do with accounts? I do not care about them, because it is entirely a matter of conscience. When a Superior knows she is administering goods that belong to the Lord, she must take care of them. Is it not so? Your conscience answers for it to God.”267

It was part of Mother Rosa’s pedagogy to warn the Superiors of their mistakes, but she did so with great discernment!

“My daughter, do not be anxious about what I wrote to you, because you must know that I am not displeased with you, no, my daughter; you must understand that my advice is not a reproof, it is a suggestion; all my advice is for your good and for the good of our dear Institute. Is it not so?”268

She did not fail to express approval and praise: “Well done! You have done everything well. I am very pleased,” and other similar expressions. She expressed approval and shared joy, in a crescendo of tenderness:

“There is no need for me to tell you, because I know how shrewd you are in everything. Well done, I am very pleased with your work. As for paying accounts, go slowly, for little by little you will see that you will lack nothing; the girls will grow and you will find yourself able to make some savings, so your heart will be fully satisfied, is it not so? Courage and do not be discouraged. Be cheerful, and in all your needs ask the advice of your poor Mother, who will always help you.”269

The Mother naturally sees the wider dimension of her Daughters. In fact the Lord granted her the joy of seeing her desires fulfilled, and she discovered in the Daughters the marvelous traits of grace that made them authentic Daughters of St. Anne. And this was a great joy for her Mother’s heart.

“What great consolation your work is to me! Well done! I clearly see that the Holy Mother has given you the true spirit and everything grows in you. So courage! I shall always pray that you may reach holiness and be a true champion of the Institute.”270

Motherhood, a gift for the “mission”

The mystical experience of fiery union with God, the essence of love, is for Rosa Gattorno total and a dynamic energy. It mobilizes all the resources of heart, mind and body toward the aspiration to share in the irresistible flame of love that welled up from the depth of her being:

“I feel in me (something) that I have never felt, that makes me burn and consumes me wholly. It makes me understand, it fills my mind with great and wonderful thoughts; I feel that I am and have everything in my Love… My Good, I will never cease to speak and write of you, and if I had to, I would run through the streets crying out to everyone to stop offending you and to try only your love.”271

She now feels herself caught up in the love of her Good, which transforms everything that is in her into vital force and action. Nothing can stop her, no obstacle within or outside her can slow her course; the vital force springs from her total belonging to him, she is wholly gift as response, concentrated in the one principle; she will go everywhere crying out to all with a voice that is no longer her own. The vital flow she transmits is that of her Good. She acts in him, for him and with him. Her voice is the voice of God, the word that penetrates hearts, converts them and turns them to God. Mother Rosa desires no other reward and no other rest than to have what she loves. In this language Rosa Gattorno reveals herself as a perfect woman and mother. She tends, with her own reality, to bring her life to other lives, until she is consumed, and moreover she gives her wholeness by increasing her capacity to love. After exhausting all her energies, she feels that she has not given everything. The more she experiences the joy of life at the source (“nothing of this valley of tears can satisfy me”), the more she feels sent to cry out to all the Good News that God is the only Good. She questions herself, asks God what she must do.

“What can I do to make you known? How can I convert so many souls who today do not believe? Oh, a thousand lives I would give to be able to convert the whole world, and slowly I would consume them.”272

God had already given her an answer, by calling her to his Work, inviting her every day into his field of work. He had helped her to become Mother of many Daughters, and her water drawn from the Source flowed from the depth of her soul into others, and like an effective and beneficial network of channels irrigated the soil of the hearts of men and women, so that life might flourish in them. Her Daughters, united to her by a unique bond of love, are like an extension of Mother Rosa:

“This poor mother of yours bears you a great affection, and it is such that only dear Jesus could show you how great its measure is! Oh! Suffice it to say that I want you a saint, and when this nourishes the soul, it is certainly necessary to be always held close to the Heart of Jesus our Love. Love is ingenious, it seeks nothing else than to please the beloved, so that nothing pleases our Beloved except being loved. So we must try everything to make him loved and served by all the world. Here, my daughter, is the moral: that, since I want you a saint, one day you may come to sanctify the whole world!”273

To make room for the Holy Spirit, to open oneself to infinite vitality, to discover the meaning of life, to become pupils of love, seeking and inventing what pleases the Beloved: every means must be sought, with new and ever active creativity; every method and every means must be used to make him loved and served by all the world. It is important to know how to create love within us, to know how to establish new relationships and create new ways of proclamation, offering the total experience of being in communion and in harmony with love. Mother Rosa advised Sr. Irene Carmeli, one of the teaching Sisters of the school of the Parrocchietta in Rome:

“As regards the Congregation (of the Daughters of Mary) you must not show yourself timid but rather all fire for the Congregation of Mary, animating the enrolled members. The same for the schools… Show yourself capable, docile; in short, the spirit of the Institute must be on your face, is it not so, my daughter? So courage, strength and love of God; always think of Jesus, try to do everything in God’s presence, and in everything try to be humble, thinking that whatever good you do will have been done by our dear Master Jesus, who in his infinite goodness deigns to lower himself and do for us what, being such petty creatures, we cannot do.”274

To be always in God’s presence, to be ever more humble, to make room for our dear Master Jesus… who deigns… who gives us his continual renewal of a deep and intimate contact with the essence of life, in the gift of a continual motherhood. One must know how to be a manifestation and sign of this inexhaustible motherhood and know how to get involved.

“Love dear Jesus very much and then be cheerful, so that you may draw all to follow you in the apostolate of the conversion of souls.”275

“I recommend that you edify: so you will attract all the young women of the town; courage, because for Jesus everything is little.”276

To edify, to attract all the young women with the significant witness of the primacy of God’s love, with the strength and courage that spring from a life wholly given to him. It is important to extend God’s Kingdom of love, without pause and without ever turning back:

“We must not lose heart, but be courageous: fight and conquer. Forward; we must conquer for love of Jesus.”277

This militant style does not contradict her motherhood. It is its development and fulfillment in the exuberance and fullness of life that tends to overcome everything that is evil and hostile, that opposes the love of Jesus. That opposes him, who is LIFE.

4.6.1. For the “propagation of the faith”

- To make God known, loved and served everywhere

“I will run everywhere” is her inspiration. Therefore she sends her Daughters, a heart that loves, to cry out to all, without distinction of race and religion, the news of God’s love and goodness, of his mercy, and to be a gift of mercy. Her words are a force that drives to action.

“Courage, it is a time of work and of great mission, of winning souls for God! Too many souls fall into the abyss of hell! Courage! Blood for blood. Jesus on the Cross is all torn, so are we. Is it not so?”278

To reach everyone is an unavoidable mission, confirmed by holy Church in the words of the Holy Father Pius IX.

“The Daughter of St. Anne must be an apostle who preaches the faith by good works and example to those who are Christian, to animate them even more, and seeks to convert those who are not Christian, helping them, if possible, to become so.”279

She prepares the Sisters and encourages them to study and to obtain recognized teaching qualifications, so that in school, besides instructing and educating, they may teach love of the true God, of the Church and of the Vicar of Christ.

“What consolation!” she writes to Fr. Agostino Donadio, “we have received so many girls into our community: what great mercy God has for this foundation! We are already beginning to take them into the house, taking them away from sin.”280

She wants her Daughters vigilant and full of zeal in teaching Christian doctrine. They are called to be loving mothers of young people, to nourish their bodies, to make them grow healthy, and their spirits, to make them true and good Catholics. She writes to the superior and recommends:
